subject: Private deployment: evidence request & uptime responsibility for Everwell Analytics
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@everwell.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Miguel Torres <m.torres@everwell.ai>, Everwell Legal <legal@everwell.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment — uptime attribution + evidence we can provide

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the call this morning. We want to get ahead of the SLA language for our Private deployment (VPC + customer-managed edge proxies) — specifically how Redwood will attribute uptime/latency responsibility when incidents touch components we control.

High-level ask: we need a written carveout/addendum that:
- Clearly lists what Everwell is responsible for (edge proxies, customer KMS, peering links) vs Redwood (inference runtime, node-level availability inside the VPC package).
- Defines required evidence and timelines for attribution (packet captures, KMS logs, traceroutes).
- Outlines fallback behavior (model downgrade, region failover) and any temporary credits/SLAs while we fix infra changes.

We understand some items are operational details; to help move quickly, attached two items we can share now: a screenshot of our KMS config and a recent short network trace showing a 300ms hop visible at our edge. We can provide more traces and a runbook if that helps.

Attachments: everwell_kms_config.png, network-trace-sample.pcap

Can Redwood send a checklist of the exact artifacts and acceptance criteria you need to consider an incident 'customer-attributable'? Also: is there an interim SLA you would accept while we complete an edge redesign?

Best,
Samira Khan
Head of Platform, Everwell Analytics
samira.khan@everwell.ai

Samira — thanks for the clear summary and the artifacts. This is a good starting point.

Short answers up front:
- Yes: we can propose an addendum that lays out a tight shared-responsibility matrix and a list of evidentiary items that support Customer-attributable incidents.
- Yes: we can propose an interim SLA (reduced liability for a specified period) while you complete the edge redesign, but we need exact acceptance criteria for any credits.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal sync with SRE and Legal (cc'd) to draft suggested language and the evidence checklist.
2) Redwood will return a draft addendum and a sample runbook/acceptance checklist within 3 business days.
3) We’ll iterate with Everwell ops on a final evidence list (format + retention window).

Can you also confirm the time windows when KMS rotations happen (daily/weekly) and whether you have a maintenance calendar we can reference for attribution? That will affect acceptable evidence (e.g., KMS audit logs with TTL).

I’m looping in Vivek, Karthik and Priya to own the addendum and evidence packaging.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

Naomi — thanks. Quick answers:
- KMS rotations: monthly by default; immediate rotations occasionally for emergency keys. We retain audit logs for 90 days.
- Maintenance windows: Sat 02:00–04:00 UTC weekly for edge updates. We’ll annotate the calendar and share a link.

I’m attaching the two files from the first note again and a short runbook we use for our edge team (MVP fallback steps) — that should show the mechanics of how we roll forward/back changes.

We would appreciate Redwood drafting language that:
- Allows us to be credited for verified customer-attributable downtime but sets a maximum credit cap during the interim (e.g., 10% monthly credit) while we remediate.
- Specifies the exact artifacts Redwood requires to accept customer-attribution:
  * packet captures around the incident window (pcap)
  * KMS audit log entries with request IDs
  * traceroute/mtr outputs and timestamps
  * short-lived signed runbook excerpts showing operator actions

Attachments: network-trace-sample.pcap, mvp-fallback-runbook.pdf, everwell_kms_config.png

Let us know if you need these in a particular format (e.g., zipped with checksums).

Best,
Samira

Thanks Naomi — draft language below I think will work as a first pass. I’ll own the SRE acceptance criteria; Karthik/Priya can refine the commercial/compliance bits.

Suggested SLA addendum excerpt (draft):
"Operational Boundary and Attribution. For Private deployments, Customer is responsible for the operation and availability of components explicitly designated as Customer-managed (including, but not limited to: edge proxies, customer-managed KMS instances, and customer-configured peering links). Redwood is responsible for the availability and performance of the inference runtime and associated nodes deployed as part of the Private package.

Attribution Process and Evidence Requirements. When an incident potentially involves both Customer-managed and Redwood-managed components, Redwood will: (a) open a joint investigation and request the following artifacts from Customer within 72 hours of incident detection: packet captures (pcap) spanning the incident window, KMS audit logs with request IDs, traceroute/mtr outputs with timestamps and probes to Redwood ingress, and signed runbook excerpts documenting operator actions during the incident window; (b) accept gzipped pcap files accompanied by SHA256 checksums; and (c) produce an attribution report within 5 business days of receipt of required artifacts.

Interim Credit During Remediation. If Customer demonstrates with accepted artifacts that the incident was customer-attributable, Redwood will credit the Customer per the following interim schedule while the Customer completes remediation: up to a 10% service credit on the impacted month’s usage for verified customer-attributable incidents, not to exceed a total of 25% across any 3-month rolling period.

Fallback and Availability Controls. Redwood will make available two mitigation options during joint incidents: (1) model-downgrade to a lower-throughput variant to preserve availability, and (2) region-failover where compatible and permitted by network topology. Any mitigation executed by Redwood will be documented and included in the attribution report.
"

Operational acceptance criteria (SRE):
- PCAPs must include timestamps and packet-level headers showing hops between customer edge and Redwood ingress; missing timestamps or truncated captures may be rejected.
- KMS logs must include request IDs and UTC timestamps; logs older than retention window must be explained with retention policy.
- Traceroutes should be run at 1m intervals for a 15m baseline when possible; single-sample traceroutes are acceptable for emergent events but may lengthen attribution time.

Next steps: I’ll turn this into a one-page addendum and share a tracked-change doc for Legal/Karthik. Naomi — can you share the HubSpot record and get Everwell to confirm the maintenance calendar link?

— Vivek
VP, Site Reliability, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
